title: Artist or illustrator
summary: For artists and illustrators: the work fills the page, then how to commission you and where to buy prints.

notFor: Studios selling many products (start from small-business)

cards.purpose: Six to twelve pieces that show their range.
How commissions work and how to start one.
Optional: where to buy prints or originals.
Process, clients and what a commission costs.

slots.ask: What name do you want at the top of the page?
slots.write: Exactly as they give it. Never shorten or translate it.

slots.ask: In one line, what do you do and for whom?
slots.write: One sentence, at most 120 characters, no hashtags or emoji.

slots.ask: Do you want a place on your profile? A city or region is enough.
slots.write: As they write it. Never infer it.

slots.ask: Do you have a website of your own?
Do you have a square photo or logo for your profile picture?
slots.write: The member uploads it in the editor; never fetch one from the web.

slots.ask: Which six to twelve pieces best show your work now?
slots.write: They upload each piece in the editor. Alt = what the piece shows, from their own description; caption = title, medium, and client or year.

slots.ask: Are you open to commissions? How should people start one?
slots.write: Heading = open or closed, as they say; text = what they take on and response time. Email: Only an address they confirm may be public: everyone can see it.

slots.ask: Do you sell prints or originals anywhere?
slots.write: Shop URLs with a label and one line on what is sold there; social accounts as URL only.

slots.ask: What media do you work in, who have you worked for, and do you publish commission prices?
slots.write: One line on their media, then bold-labelled lines. Prices only if they publish them; clients only if they may be named.
